t: G33 UAV Engine: Fixed-Wing Lift Desk — Simple
name: G33 UAV Engine: Fixed-Wing Lift Desk — Simple
title: G33 UAV Engine: Fixed-Wing Lift Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Lift must equal weight: L = ½ρv²S·CL. The desk computes the stall speed from wing loading and the cruise lift from the polar — the airframe either closes the budget or it doesn't fly.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Lift at 15 m/s, S=0.5 m², CL=0.8, sea level = 55.1 N. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: The Perpetual UAV Engine (G33) – Quantifying the Autonomous Flight Constant (AFC)
real_world_basis: The lift equation is the real, universal basis of winged flight.
signature_version: Signature version: the AFC lift desk — the chapter's Autonomous Flight Constant as the efficiency target (L/D), with the 'perpetual' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: weigh everything, then size the wing to the weight.
math_note: Lift at 15 m/s, S=0.5 m², CL=0.8, sea level: 55.1 N [verified]; Weight of a 5 kg airframe: 49.1 N [verified]

math_check.label: Lift at 15 m/s, S=0.5 m², CL=0.8, sea level
Weight of a 5 kg airframe

safety: Flight safety: test-glide unpowered first; never maiden over people.
how_it_works: Plug in air density, cruise speed, wing area, and lift coefficient; verify lift ≥ weight with margin. The demo checks a 5 kg airframe.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact

title: G33 UAV Engine: Endurance Calculator — Compounded
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Endurance = battery energy / power draw, derated for the reserve. The calculator applies the 20% reserve rule and the Peukert-ish reality that high draws deliver less — the flight time is computed, then flight-tested.

Compounding view. Headline number: Endurance: 80 Wh usable at 150 W = 32.0 min. This tier combines the mechanism with its limits: what is real engineering today, what the Signature version adds, and where the boundary sits.
chapter_source: The Perpetual UAV Engine (G33) – Quantifying the Autonomous Flight Constant (AFC)
real_world_basis: Energy-over-power endurance math is real and universal.
signature_version: Signature version: the AFC endurance desk — the chapter's constant as the endurance frontier, with the perpetual framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: bench-test the power draw before trusting the calculation.
math_note: Endurance: 80 Wh usable at 150 W: 32.0 min [verified]; Kinetic energy of 2 kg at 20 m/s: 400 J [verified]

math_check.label: Endurance: 80 Wh usable at 150 W
Kinetic energy of 2 kg at 20 m/s

safety: Flight safety: land at the reserve, not at empty — the reserve is inviolable.
how_it_works: Divide usable energy by cruise power, apply the reserve, and report the planned endurance with the test tolerance. The demo plans a mapping sortie.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact
Every numerical claim recomputed at build time

t: G33 UAV Engine: Link Budget Desk — Simple
name: G33 UAV Engine: Link Budget Desk — Simple
title: G33 UAV Engine: Link Budget Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] The radio link closes or it doesn't: received power = transmit + gains − losses, and the margin over the receiver threshold is the link budget. The desk computes the margin at max range — control without margin is a flyaway waiting to happen.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Shannon capacity of a 1 MHz link at SNR 7 = 3.00 Mbps. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: The Perpetual UAV Engine (G33) – Quantifying the Autonomous Flight Constant (AFC)
real_world_basis: Link-budget arithmetic is the real basis of every radio system.
signature_version: Signature version: the AFC link desk — the chapter's constant as the margin target, with the perpetual framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: range-test on the ground before flying the full distance.
math_note: Shannon capacity of a 1 MHz link at SNR 7: 3.00 Mbps [verified]; Free-space path loss at 5 km, 2.4 GHz: 2.527e+11 ratio [verified]

math_check.label: Shannon capacity of a 1 MHz link at SNR 7
Free-space path loss at 5 km, 2.4 GHz

safety: Flight safety: set the failsafe (return-to-home) before the first flight — always.
how_it_works: Add transmit power and antenna gains, subtract free-space and system losses at max range, compare to receiver sensitivity. The demo budgets a 5 km link.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact

t: G33 UAV Engine: Autonomy Stack — Simple
name: G33 UAV Engine: Autonomy Stack — Simple
title: G33 UAV Engine: Autonomy Stack — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Autonomy is a stack: state estimation, guidance, and control, each with its update rate and error bound. The stack specs the sensor rates from the Nyquist rule against the vehicle's dynamics — the estimator must sample faster than the physics it tracks.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Nyquist rate for 50 Hz airframe dynamics = 100 Hz. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

real_world_basis: Estimator-controller stacks are the real architecture of autonomous flight.
signature_version: Signature version: the AFC autonomy stack — the chapter's constant as the autonomy-level target, with the perpetual framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: get manual flight solid before enabling any autonomy.
math_note: Nyquist rate for 50 Hz airframe dynamics: 100 Hz [verified]; Amdahl speedup, 80% parallel, 8x cores: 3.33 x [verified]

math_check.label: Nyquist rate for 50 Hz airframe dynamics
Amdahl speedup, 80% parallel, 8x cores

safety: Flight safety: the manual override must work faster than the autonomy can fail.
how_it_works: Set the control bandwidth from the airframe dynamics, double it twice for the estimator rate (Nyquist plus margin), and pick sensors that deliver it. The demo rates an IMU/GPS stack.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
